utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecution versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the next witness is Major Angus Hay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are we ready to call him?

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness, yes, is waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: While we are waiting for him, I notice that some of the evidence which he gives is purely corroborative of other evidence. I have in mind, Mr. Lopez-Terres, paragraphs 12 to 18, which deal with the meeting between Colonel Stewart and Colonel Blaskic concerning Ahmici; paragraphs 35 to 46, which relate to the Convoy of Joy; and paragraphs 53 to 64, which deal with the attack on Grbavica. Perhaps you could take those matters fairly shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If you'd like to sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may. We have previously informed counsel for the Prosecution that we do not object to the Prosecution leading this witness with respect to all paragraphs, except for, in the case of Mr. Kordic, paragraphs 30 to 34. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We do the same, and we only ask to avoid leading questions related to the paragraphs 19 to 27.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lopez-Terres. Examined by Mr. Lopez-Terres:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are Major Angus Hay, born in 1967?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You joined the British army in 1983, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the end of April 1993, when you were a Captain with the British army, you were attached to the Prince of Wales Regiment, which had -- which arrived at the time to Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You succeeded Captain Matthew Dundas-Whatley, who came from the Cheshire Regiment; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You discharged the duties of the liaison officer with the Prince of Wales Regiment; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, you were based at the British Battalion compound which was in Nova Bila?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the beginning of your work, your area of responsibility included Busovaca, Vitez, Zenica Novi Travnik, Travnik, and Turbe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And shortly it transpired that this area of responsibility was too large for one liaison officer, so in June 1993 that area was divided, was partitioned, and you became responsible for Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Turbe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The area of Vitez itself was the responsibility of Captain Lee Whitworth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the initial days when you took over, Captain Dundas-Whatley introduced you to various commanders in Central Bosnia and you also visited those individuals?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of this visit, you had an opportunity of meeting with Colonel Blaskic, who was responsible for the Central Bosnian Operative Zone, and you also were told that Mario Cerkez was the commander of the local brigade in Vitez and that Colonel Blaskic was his superior?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were with Colonel Stewart when you met Colonel Blaskic, and it was after the events in Ahmici. Now, could you tell us: How did Colonel Blaskic react when Colonel Stewart spoke to him about the events in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: The first time that I was introduced to Colonel Blaskic by Captain Dundas-Whatley followed the immediate aftermath of Ahmici. We were in the throes of our handover/takeover at the time, and during the course of the meeting, Colonel Bob Stewart, who was commander of the Cheshire BritBat at the time, came into the meeting, sort of crashed into the meeting, and he was quite emotional, and he started -- or I do recall him saying to Colonel Blaskic, "Tihomir, you're going to have to answer for what's happened in Ahmici," to which Colonel Blaskic, as I recall, didn't really respond, didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're still in May 1993. At that time, you were asked to accompany two U.N. representatives who were visiting the area of Vitez and Busovaca and conducting investigations about what had happened in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with these U.N. representatives, you went to Colonel Blaskic's headquarters in the Vitez Hotel and, once again, the question about what had been done in Ahmici was raised. Could you briefly tell us: How did Colonel Blaskic respond or react when he was asked questions about the incident -- about the attacks in Ahmici by those United Nations representatives?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: When we visited -- when I visited Colonel Blaskic again with the two U.N. representatives, Colonel Blaskic denied all responsibility, as I recall, and said at the same time that he had instigated his own investigation into the events surrounding the tragedy at Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in Central Bosnia until November 1993. During that time, were you advised about the results of any investigation conducted by the HVO and the arrest or perhaps -- about the arrest of the perpetrators of the attack on Ahmici or perhaps whether they had been brought to justice?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No. As far as I was told, as far as I remember, there was no results from those investigations that Colonel Blaskic said he was going to conduct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Hay, you do not remember, do you, the names of the two United Nations investigators, do you? But I should like to show you some photographs so that you could tell us if you can again recognise either of the two U.N. representatives in these photographs, whom you escorted. It is photographs 1576.1, 1576.3. Could you please have a look at those photographs.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: As I said, I can't remember their names, and I can't remember the 1576.1 and 2, but I do remember the individual in 1576.3 and 1576.4. As I say, I can't remember his name, but I do recall him, recall that he was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to draw the attention of the Chamber that photographs 1576.1 and 2 are the photographs of Payam Akhavan, who already testified in this case, and the other two photographs show the second investigator, Thomas Osario.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't anticipate there is any dispute about any of this, yes. So let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Hay, after your visit to Colonel Blaskic, you escorted these two representatives to the headquarters of the Vitez brigade, and there you met Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was present in Mario Cerkez's office when you came to see him?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: As we arrive -- as we arrived, I remember in the back of the room that there was an individual whom I came to know as Darko Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that meeting, did perhaps the presence of that person appear intimidating or threatening to you or to the representatives of the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: The two representatives from the United Nations were exceedingly apprehensive and unsettled by his presence, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how that man whom you identify as Darko Kraljevic was dressed? What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: As I recall, he was in dark clothing and -- as a lot of people tended to be out there, but even he more so, sort of armed to the hilt, basically; very overtly armed and very intimidating. And I think that's why the United Nations representatives found it all the more overbearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you and the U.N. investigators told why Darko Kraljevic was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the one who organised that meeting, weren't you, at the time, when asked to do so by the U.N. investigators?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I did. I would have made it a day in advance or a couple of days in advance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember inviting Darko Kraljevic to the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No. I didn't even know who that individual was at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the investigators who were with you who could have invited Darko Kraljevic to attend the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, they wouldn't have known who he was either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you think, who invited Darko Kraljevic to attend the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that is really too leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Major, do you have any idea about that, or not? When I say "idea," do you have any knowledge, as opposed to speculation?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No? Thank you. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to show you two photographs, Major Hay. Could you please tell us if you recognise the person on these two photographs. This is Z1680,1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's Darko Kraljevic. And that's him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is that individual whom you saw in Mario Cerkez's office during the meeting that we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that meeting, the question of Ahmici was raised. Could you tell us, what was Mario Cerkez's response when he was asked about his possible responsibility for the acts committed in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: He denied any involvement in Ahmici altogether, and indeed actually turned around and said it was probably the BiH that did it themselves in order that the HVO would get the blame. But then he did say afterwards he would conduct his own investigation as well, or initiate an investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that meeting with Mario Cerkez and Darko Kraljevic, did you have an opportunity to meet -- to see Darko Kraljevic again?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that at the time, my area of responsibility was going to be handed over sort of in the succeeding couple of weeks, but -- during my tour around Vitez and visits to Mario Cerkez's office, again, I do remember seeing that individual in and around the area of the cinema on a couple of occasions, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "cinema," you mean the headquarters of Mario Cerkez, is it?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that visit to Colonel Blaskic and Mario Cerkez, did you accompany U.N. investigators when they met with other authorities in Central Bosnia, and in particular with Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the exercise of your duty and while you were responsible for the area of Novi Travnik, you also came across the name of Jozo Leutar, who was placed in charge of that area by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right. He was the local commander in Travnik. He took over from a chap who was there when I first arrived, who I cannot recall his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you were posted to this new area, you already had an opportunity of going to Busovaca and also meeting with local commanders there?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was Mr. Grubesic, was it?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: He was the -- he was the local commander in Busovaca, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember what that gentleman was wearing when you met him?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I do recall that he used to be predominantly dressed in black; black overalls, if I remember rightly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also had an opportunity of meeting Dario Kordic. Could you please describe the circumstances under which that happened? In Busovaca, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It was when I was giving -- I use the term "office call" to the -- Grubesic in Busovaca, and Dario Kordic arrived with two individuals, came into the office, and I think it was just for introductions, really, to meet me. I wasn't aware of the meeting beforehand or anything. But we were introduced on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Dario Kordic arrived there with two persons. Could you tell us, who, or rather what were those two persons?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I presumed, from the way that they were dressed and the fact that Dario Kordic certainly didn't overtly carry any weapons, that they were -- I interpreted them to be bodyguards, basically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember what Dario Kordic was wearing on that first occasion when you met?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: He was in uniform, in sort of -- in HVO uniform. But I do recall that he had a wooden cross around his -- around his neck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Dario Kordic came to that office in Busovaca, you did not really know what he was, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No. But he certainly had a -- had a presence, certainly, to the -- to the rest of the HVO sort of soldiers around him. They obviously held him in some regard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you notice anything in particular, how he behaved, how he treated -- how they treated Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: With respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you briefly tell us about the second occasion when you saw Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It was not long after this event, and we had been invited to a cabin just to the sort of south -- south-west, south-east, I can't remember -- of Busovaca, way up a track. And it was really a social event, and it was really the first occasion for the new commander of BritBat, Colonel Alastair Duncan, to meet the local sort of Croat leaders, HVO commanders, in and around the Lasva Valley. At that meeting there was Colonel Blaskic with his wife; there was Dario Kordic with his two people, two bodyguards, basically, if I remember; there was Grubesic from Busovaca with another individual whom I cannot remember; there was Colonel Duncan with his interpreter; myself and my interpreter; and a couple of individuals from Vitez in civilian clothes. Santic was there, if I remember rightly, and, as I say, a couple of other local dignitaries, councillors or whatever they were. I cannot remember their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We shall now move on to another incident which happened somewhat later, that is, in June 1993, about something at the time was called the Convoy of Joy. Just in a few words, Major, can you tell us what did you establish about the circumstances under which the convoy was diverted?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It was no secret that there was a convoy coming up, as we called it then, at Route Diamond, and it was apprehended, stopped at the Novi Travnik -- Novi Travnik sort of junction into Novi Travnik by women with sort of sticks and goodness knows what. They stopped the whole convoy. We were aware of it, but our mandate prevented us from doing anything at that time, and unfortunately we were sort of caught between a brick and a hard place, or a rock and a hard place, and as soon as it stopped, a number of drivers were dragged, taken out of their cabs and allegedly shot straightaway. I didn't see it, but a couple of the BritBat soldiers said they couldn't believe it, and they had witnessed it. Immediately following that there was a bit of an all-for-one spree as the locals came out of the woodwork, basically, and started stripping a lot of the trucks and taking goods left, right, and centre. And a couple of trucks, individuals trucks, were taken away, were driven off by Croats or HVO soldiers, I don't remember which, but certainly I saw a number of people in civilian clothing just having a free-for-all, just helping themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see the presence of people in uniform near the convoy at the moment when it was being diverted?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes. There were a number of supposedly HVO soldiers in and around the area, and I remember asking them, can't they stop it. They said they could not, you know, they were powerless against the women. I would suggest, rather, they would not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether HVO soldiers were overpowered by members of your regiment on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Sorry, could you say that again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether HVO soldiers were beaten by soldiers belonging to your regiment?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, not beaten by --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Killed. Were they killed?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes. They -- the convoy was eventually allowed to move on again. A semblance of order was established, and we led the convoy through the Lasva Valley past Vitez. But en route towards Nova Bila, I heard that a couple of HVO soldiers had taken an RPG and came out to the lead Warrior vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You have to tell us what an RPG is.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Rocket-propelled grenade. And in self-defence they engaged the two individuals and killed them, I believe. But the convoy came to a halt, and again it came under fire from the sort of Croat community or HVO soldiers, and again a number of vehicles were stolen and a number of individuals, I think, were wounded in that encounter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may comment regarding the translation. My question was whether the soldiers were killed, not beaten, as was translated, and this caused some confusion with the witness. The French word used was"abattoir," "killed," and not "beaten." In your zone of responsibility, from September 1993 until you left, you were able to notice that the warring parties had established a kind of wall consisting of big boards that separated the two opposing forces from the north-east of Novi Travnik to the south-west of Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes. There was a dividing line all the way down through the centre of Novi Travnik that divided the ethnic groups, sort of the Muslims and the Croat/Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that passing close to this area you were able to note that there were a certain number of individuals digging trenches with tools, under the control of HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It was as I was driving through the line of conflict to get -- to go up and see the local BiH commander. I do recall seeing some individual civilians digging trenches, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were indeed under the control of HVO soldiers wearing uniform?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also remember that as you were passing close to this group, HVO soldiers tried to conceal these persons who were digging trenches from sight so that you wouldn't see them?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right. As I drove past, they sort of quickly got them down and tried to usher them out of sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You noticed on the chests and back of the people digging trenches certain objects that looked rather strange to you?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right. As I drove past and as they were being ushered out of sight, I recall seeing they did have something that was very unusual strapped to them, strapped to their backs and their sort of torso. I wasn't going to hang around; I was sort of crossing an active front line, and I drove through. On visiting the local BiH commander, Beslim Zurapi, I put this to him, asked him what was going on, and he confirmed, yes, that they had explosive devices attached to them and that they were digging trenches for the HVO. I asked who they were, and I presumed that they were Muslim, but given his indifference and his response in which he said, "If they're digging trenches for the HVO, then we will just shoot them," I didn't think he would shoot his own side, so I drew a conclusion from that that they were possibly Serbs, but they were certainly doing it under duress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons who were digging the trenches were exposed to fire from the BH army, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, from what I could see as I drove through. But moreover, Beslim Zurapi confirmed that and said, "Yes, we can see them digging the trenches and we will shoot them."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You noticed that there were wires coming out of these objects on the chest and the back of these people?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes. That was all part of the -- as I drove past, that's one of the bits that sort of stuck out, that drew my attention to it. It was if they were sort of -- wires come back into the buildings, basically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion, roughly at the same time, to discuss these matters with the local HVO commander, Zeljko Sabljic?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and he denied it. He denied all knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around the 8th of September, 1993, Major, you were at your camp in Nova Bila when a neighbouring village known as Grbavica was attacked. Could you, in a few words, tell us what you saw in the course of that attack, in a few words?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: The assault started with suppressive fire, with indirect or, rather, direct anti-tank weapon fire and heavy machine-gun fire, and then it followed the sequence of an infantry assault as the soldiers came through and swept through the village, just clearing the whole village. They also were assisted with their own improvised weaponry, notably a system called the BeBe, which is sort of a fire extinguisher packed with explosives and launched from an improvised launcher, which was quite destructive in its own right, and they cleared the whole village, basically. As far as I'm concerned, there were BiH soldiers in there, notably a sniper in the house above our officers' mess in Nova Bila, so it could be construed as a legitimate military target, but the offshoot of that was as well that the Croat families were moved in to occupy houses that still were standing at the end of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to show you a document, Major. It is a photograph with the reference number Z2036, 2036. This photograph, does it show the device that you have described to us that was known as a BeBe? Could you show it to us, please?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That there [indicates] is a launcher for the BeBe. A bit of imagination is required, but basically you just stuff the fire extinguisher in the top there, and there is an explosive primer in the bottom and it launches it a distance of a couple hundred yards. Probably a maximum of 300 yards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You yourself took this photograph, didn't you, Major?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This type of launchers for BeBes, were they widespread in the region of Novi Travnik where you were on duty?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I wouldn't just say Novi Travnik. They were used throughout the Lasva Valley. I wouldn't like to say how many there were. They weren't common, but they were around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the village of Grbavica was cleansed by the HVO. Was it originally a military target?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has given his view about that, explained that there was a sniper there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to specify the following: The cleansing of that village, did it appear to you, as a military man, to be justified by purely military goals?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It could be considered a military target, yes, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The destruction effected in the village, did it all affect military targets only?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, it didn't. The feature itself was a military target, but then what ensued afterwards, i.e., the wanton -- the burning and destruction of everything that was in there, basically, less a few houses, then that went beyond the call of military requirements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of October 1993, Major, you had occasion around October to visit General Alagic in Travnik in his headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You noticed in the basement of these headquarters the presence of HVO prisoners. Could you tell us what condition they appeared to be in?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, they were in reasonable fettle, given the fact that they were prisoners of war, but they were being looked after, and they didn't -- there was nothing untoward that I recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you announced your visit to General Alagic beforehand?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, he was unaware that I would be arriving, and it just came up during our meeting. And he took me down at my request and just showed me around, and during then is when I was introduced to the prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of October '93, in the region of Novi Travnik, you noticed an increase in the frequency of attacks by BH army forces, and especially the shelling of the HVO headquarters in Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also noted the presence or you heard talk of the presence of the 7th Muslim Brigade, the name that had been given to it?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that brigade, there was a special unit composed of elements considered to be alien to the region, commonly known as the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This unit was stationed in the village of Bandol, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: From the information that we had, and as I recall, that's where we believed that they sort of had established themselves, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you personally witness of an attack by this unit, and under which circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It -- I can't remember the date; it was towards the end of our tour. And the -- following the increase in frequency of attacks, and shelling of the HVO headquarters in Novi Travnik, just to the south of Novi Travnik -- I can't remember the name of the place at the moment -- again, on the main road or the main supply route that we had from Gornji Vakuf, we called it Route Diamond, a couple of miles just south of Novi Travnik, the BiH or 7 Muslim Brigade were massing -- I say "massing" their troops, congregating there in preparation for an assault. And it happened and unfortunately coincided with the southward movement of two U.N. convoys -- a Dutch convoy, if I remember rightly, and a UNHCR convoy -- and the two met. As the 7 Muslim Brigade were crossing the front line into the assault, the first convoy came through, and they received some shots into their vehicles; but the second convoy, unfortunately, one of the drivers received a fatal wound to the head and was killed instantly, and that vehicle crashed. The rest of them carried on moving south. Following that assault, I remember visiting the local HVO commanders -- not Sabljic Zeljko, but actually on the front line itself -- and I personally saw eight -- I was shown eight dead enemy to the HVO, i.e., BiH soldiers; but furthermore, they were members of the 7 Muslim Brigade, and none of them were ethnic to Bosnia. They were all foreigners, either from the Middle East or Africa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your tour of duty in the region, you were able to see that the Croats, when speaking of this Mujahedin unit, were petrified?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Certainly the local soldiers around Novi Travnik, yes, that's where I drew my conclusions there. At the mention of them, they got -- they were pretty -- pretty frightened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you informed, in the course of your mission, of the atrocities committed by this Mujahedin unit in your area?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, I can't recall. I think there was -- there were rumours, but I never had any cause to base any of it on fact, that I saw, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that ends my examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Sayers:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, please let my introduce myself. My name is Steve Sayers, and along with my colleague here, Mr. Naumovski, we represent Dario Kordic. These gentlemen are Mr. Kovacic and Mr. Mikulicic, and they represent Mr. Cerkez. Major, you've testified that you arrived in Central Bosnia in late April, I believe?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you took over as a liaison officer from the existing liaison officer with the Cheshires, Captain Matthew Dundas-Whatley?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, sir, you are actually a member of the Gordon Highlanders, I believe, and you were on detachment -- or special attachment to the Prince of Wales Own Regiment of Yorkshire?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you've testified about this, but let me be clear, sir: Initially your area of responsibility was extremely extensive? I think you'll agree with that.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you came to the conclusion that it was actually too much for one liaison officer to handle, and you brought that to your commanding officer's attention, to the attention of Lieutenant-Colonel Duncan; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understand it, sir, Captain Whitworth assumed your duties for the immediate area of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And another officer with the Prince of Wales Own, Captain Bruce Cowan, took over responsibility for Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please forgive the pauses, but we have to let the interpreters catch up, and I would appreciate it if you would just give a little bit of a pause between my question and the answer, and I'll try to do the same for you. Thank you. Would it be fair to say that in connection with your duties as liaison officer, Major, after Captains Whitworth and Cowan took over the Vitez and the Busovaca areas, your involvement with those areas was infrequent and only occasional?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's -- that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your view, sir, was Captain Dundas-Whatley a knowledgeable and capable officer, well-liked by local commanders and dignitaries, as far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: As far as I could tell, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was at the end of the Cheshires' tour and presumably imparted to you the knowledge that had been collectively gained by that regiment during the six months that they had spent in Central Bosnia, at least insofar as your initial area of responsibility was concerned; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described meeting with the local HVO military commander in Busovaca, commander Dusko Grubesic. Could you tell us how many times you actually met this commander, sir? If you can remember.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It wouldn't be more than --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, could you please come closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It -- probably -- not more than ten times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Major, I'm being told to get closer to the microphone, and I think the same goes for you. You tend to speak a little softly, so I wonder if you could just speak directly into the microphone --

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- for the interpreters' convenience. Let me just ask you a few questions in connection with the view that the Prince of Wales Own Regiment, and you as one of the people attached to that regiment for special service, gained of the chain of command of the HVO. Would it be fair to say, sir, that this subject was discussed between you and your fellow liaison officers in briefings that I believe the commanding officer held every night?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You need to turn the microphone on, sir.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Sorry. Okay, there we go. Sorry. Yes, every evening we would have a wash-up or a debrief of the day's events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the Central Bosnia area, the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, at the top of the chain of command was Colonel Blaskic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Top of the military, direct military chain of command, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you meet with Colonel Blaskic on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: During my initial days of handover, takeover, with Captain Dundas-Whatley, I tried to visit him on a daily basis, and I must have done so, probably -- give or take a day here or there, obviously -- over a period of -- maybe a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You learned, sir, that Colonel Blaskic was a professional military man with a professional military background; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I believe he was a former JNA officer, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Career officer in the --

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- in the army? And in his chain of command, sir, he reported up the chain to the general staff of the HVO in Mostar; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I -- now you're talking about things I don't really --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a level above your area --

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yeah, I wasn't -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to meet with or deal with the commander of the military police battalion headquartered in the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Not that I was aware of, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the name of a special-purpose unit called the Vitezovi ring any familiar bells with you, or is that a name that you do not recognise?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It's a name that I got to know, but after I had handed over responsibility to Captain Whitworth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the forces under Colonel Blaskic's command basically consisted of, if I may describe them this way, municipality-based or territorially-based brigades; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That was our interpretation, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And each one of these brigades had separate commanders; for example, commander Grubesic in Busovaca, who reported to Colonel Blaskic in the chain of command; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That was the interpretation, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And within the brigades, they were organised into companies, and the company commanders, as you would expect, reported up their chain of command to the brigade commanders; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's the way I would suppose it would happen, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there's no question that Colonel Blaskic had a number of these brigades under his command; he also had the military police under his command, and the special purpose units, such as the Vitezovi, which I've previously described; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Whether they were under his command or not, I don't know. I'm sorry, I can't -- I couldn't ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me turn to the first meeting that you described with Colonel Blaskic, Major. This was held at his headquarters, the HVO headquarters in the Hotel Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall Lieutenant-Colonel Stewart coming into the meeting and saying, as you've described, "Tihomir, you're going to have to answer for the actions at Ahmici"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have a clear recollection that this provoked no reaction initially or response from Colonel Blaskic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right. But immediately following that I could -- you know, I had a sort of -- I had to get on with Captain Dundas-Whatley, and we left pretty quickly after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, that Lieutenant-Colonel Duncan was also at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I can't, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you only ever had one meeting with Colonel Blaskic and Lieutenant-Colonel Stewart in the same room, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: As far as I remember, just that one occasion, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you a document and see if I can jog your memory as to who was there, if I may.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D130/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're now going to put -- this is a diary, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the point of putting a diary from somebody else to this witness? Take it back and don't mark it. You can put it to the witness who made the diary. There's no point putting it to somebody else and asking him to comment. The witness has said he doesn't recollect who else was present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may, then, Major, I'd like show you a military information summary, so-called milinfosum, milinfosum number 10 from the PWO, dated May the 9th of 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be marked D130/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, this is a document that we received last night. Does this appear to be in the regular format of military information summaries that were prepared by your regiment, as far as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It looks a similar format, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under the heading of "Vitez," Colonel [sic], item number 2, it looks as if there's something missing from this milinfosum. There appears to be a break in the date-stamp numbers on the top right-hand corner. The page is 61298. The second page appears to be 61302. So it looks like there were a couple of pages missing. There's also a reference to a meeting with Mr. Cerkez on this day. Did you attend that meeting, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I have to say -- I'm sorry -- if we're going into specific days now, I cannot remember accurately from one day to the next.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fair enough, Major. I'd just like to draw your attention to one entry on the second page, up on the top paragraph. The military information officer in the POW [sic], I take it, was Captain Harrison?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that Captain Harrison compiled these reports not based upon his own personal knowledge but based upon what liaison officers --

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- communicated to him? All right. A reference is made to a fairly heated discussion between representatives of the warring factions, and it is communicated to the military information officer that both sides implicitly acknowledge that their soldiers had conducted ethnic cleansing. Do you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't see this. Where are we reading from, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: It's page 61302, Your Honour, and it's the second sentence before the end of the first paragraph on that page. The top paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't mean to spring this on you unannounced, Major, but would it be fair to say that both the HVO and the ABiH, during your tour of duty in the Central Bosnia area, basically acknowledged that both of their -- that soldiers under their command had conducted ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I cannot recall, but I wouldn't say it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fair enough, sir. Let's move on. In connection with the questions that you were asked on direct-examination, sir, regarding whether an investigation had produced any results, an investigation into the events at Ahmici, were you aware that Colonel Blaskic had actually asked Lieutenant-Colonel Stewart to put together a multi-lateral commission consisting of representatives not only of the HVO but also of the ABiH, the Muslim side, and also the ECMM and BritBat, to do a joint investigation into the events at Ahmici? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No. I can't -- no. I wasn't privy to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that the investigators that you escorted in May of 1993, while they were conducting an investigation themselves on behalf of the U.N. Centre for Human Rights, I believe, into the events at Ahmici, were you aware that they had actually identified four individuals whom they had determined to have participated in the events at Ahmici on April the 16th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I'm -- no, I cannot recall. I wasn't privy to their sort of findings or anything. They were out there purely investigating at the time. I wasn't privy to their findings or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall being present, sir, at a meeting held on May the 13th, 1993, at which were present Lieutenant-Colonel Duncan and three political figures from Vitez: Anto Valenta, the Deputy President of the HVO or vice-president of the HVO, accompanied by Ivica Santic and Pero Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I'm sure I was present at the meeting. I can't specifically recall it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just see if I can show you a document that may or may not jog your memory. It's a milinfosum that was prepared about that meeting on that day?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Milinfosum number 14.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D131/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Appearing on the first item on this milinfosum is a description of the meeting that I discussed, with Mr. Valenta. Does this jog your memory as to whether you attended such a meeting, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: During the initial days of handover, I attended so many meetings; I'm sorry, I can't recall this specific one. There was so much going on at the time really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The contemporaneous notes that were prepared by your CO reflect that there was -- May the 13th began with a trip to the Vitez Hotel with Angus Hay to meet Valenta?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The military information summary, I assume, accurately summarised what Mr. Valenta told you and your commanding officer at the --

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That would have been the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see a reference, sir, to the 7th Muslim Brigade of the 3rd Corps of the ABiH. I think that you concluded your tour with some discussion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Would it be fair to say that you heard expressions of concern regarding the activities of this unit throughout your tour?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LOPEZ-TERRES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a comment, Mr. President. As regards the notes to which Mr. Sayers is referring, once again it is a diary which was mentioned a few moments ago, which was -- some time ago and which your Chamber refused. That was the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm not following this. Your reference, I thought, was to the milinfosum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There was a reference to Colonel Duncan's diary which contained a sentence, sir, that refers to: "Beginning the day with a trip to the Hotel Vitez with Angus Hay to meet Valenta," and my next question was whether this military information summary encapsulated the results of that meeting, and the Major, I thought, answered, "yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts are we finding it on the milinfosum?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: On the first page, Your Honour, under item 1, "Vitez area," the second paragraph. It says: "During a meeting, Anto Valenta, vice-president of the HVO OZ CB stated that he was concerned about the possibility of elements of the 7th Muslim Brigade, 3rd BiH Corps, coming into his area," and then he recites a number of statistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I missed the reference to the diary. Mr. Sayers, do not refer to the diary without specific leave. Now, let me find -- let's see what the witness says about this, which is the important thing. Major, the second paragraph of the document which we have, the milinfosum, does that accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: If it's documented, that would have been printed up at the end of the day and that's why it would have gone to print anyway. So I've got no reason to deny that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And have we this document marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: As the next Defence exhibit. It's marked D131/1, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Major. Would it be fair to say that attempts were made by the members of your unit, by the liaison officers, to communicate accurate information regarding significant developments or events or meetings to the military information officer insofar as that was possible and those events were contemporaneously or virtually contemporaneously recorded in the -- or summarised in the military information summary?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That was our modus operandi. That's the way we conducted business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have any recollection, would it be fair to say, other than what is summarised in the milinfosum that we see here, of any statements made by Messrs. Valenta, Santic, or Skopljak; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Two other items in connection with this military information summary, sir, which you may or may not be able to help us with. If you would turn to the second page. It's actually marked "3 of 5" at the top. Right at the top of the page there's a reference to the supposed movements of the 7th Muslim Brigade and the 305th Jajce Brigade. Both of these are identified as manoeuvre units of the 3rd Corps. Could you just let us know, sir, what a manoeuvre unit is? Does it have any special purpose or characteristics?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: My interpretation would be that it's a unit -- how can I put this? It's a specialist unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, I don't -- I really don't mean to put you on the spot. If the term "manoeuvre unit" doesn't have a particular meaning in terms of a term of art in your military profession, please let me know. Would it be fair to say that the observation made by the military information officer that the 3rd Corps was preparing to prosecute its tactically dominant position in the Lasva Valley as response to HVO aggressions further south, was that your tactical analysis of the situation or didn't you have one?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No. That's the intelligence officers. That's what he got paid for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One final question in connection with this milinfosum, sir. Under the third entry regarding events in Zenica, there's a reference to three abducted Croat men having been found, their bodies in a charred condition, in the basement of a burned-out house. You can also read what else is stated in that paragraph, and there's no need to repeat. Suffice it to say, sir, that this is the kind of incident that would have been discussed by you and your colleagues at the commanders' briefing held during the evening of May the 13th or shortly thereafter; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, but at the same -- I mean, I say -- we had a meeting in the evenings, and then anybody who had any specific information would then go and have a one-to-one with the intelligence officer thereafter. So we weren't always privy to what everybody was going on or knowing what everybody else was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever aware of any investigations that were initiated by the ABiH in connection with that particular incident, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly regarding the command structure in Travnik, which was covered by your area of responsibility. You mentioned that early on during your tour the HVO commander was replaced but you could not remember the name of the first commander.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I suggest to you that the name was Colonel Filip Filipovic, does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was the --

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- commander? And the second commander was Jozo Leutar?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Mr. Leutar?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't hear that he had actually been appointed Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs for the federation and was blown up in a car bomb in Sarajevo rather recently?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last year, in fact. You didn't know that, I take it.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the subject of Mr. Kordic, sir, as you were being taken around and being introduced by Captain Dundas-Whatley, you were introduced to Mr. Kordic, and I believe your testimony was you were not sure how he fitted into the overall picture; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's -- that was my conclusions at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that that was the conclusion of the liaison officer who was taking you around and introducing you to various local figures, Captain Dundas-Whatley?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I cannot remember what his opinion was, but -- I can't remember what his opinion was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's fair to say, sir, that you rarely, if ever, saw Colonel Blaskic and Mr. Kordic together; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout your tour of duty, I believe you never actually saw Mr. Kordic at the HVO headquarters in the Hotel Vitez; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I can't recall ever seeing him there; correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it also be fair to say that you did not attend any of the weekly press conferences held by the politicians and military leaders of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, I didn't attend those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it also be fair to say that your knowledge of Mr. Kordic's position at the end of your tour did not differ markedly from your knowledge of Colonel Blaskic's and Mr. Kordic's position at the beginning of your tour?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you attended a luncheon at a cabin to the south of Busovaca, south-east or south-west, but to the south of Busovaca in May, I believe, of 1993, along with your CO, some local dignitaries, and Colonel Blaskic and Commander Grubesic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right. Pretty soon after I arrived in theatre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it, sir, that that was the only luncheon that you ever attended at which your CO, Lieutenant-Colonel Duncan, and Mr. Kordic were present?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's the only one that I was present at when those two were present, yes, that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall also being present a representative of DutchBat, the Dutch battalion of UNPROFOR, Colonel Paulus Schipper, I think his name is?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: The commander of the Dutch battalion. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And it would be fair to say that you do not recall anything of particular political or military significance being discussed at this luncheon because it was a purely social event designed to get people to --

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I think it was predominantly the introduction of the new commanding officer of BritBat to the local dignitaries and commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, whether Colonel Blaskic's second in command, Franjo Nakic, was also present at this luncheon?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I cannot remember. There were a number of other individuals there, a couple of other individuals, but I can't remember who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I wonder if I could just show you a copy of a milinfosum, number 20, dated May the 19th, 1993. It may or may not make reference to this meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D132/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just two or three questions in connection with this milinfosum, sir. In the centre of the first paragraph, under item 1, "Vitez," the military information officer records that: "When both Blaskic and his deputy, Nakic, were independently appraised that the fire," sniper fire, I think they're referring to, "was uncomfortably close," once again to the BritBat compound, I believe, "and that the guard might return fire, they agreed that this was the only means of resolving the problem." Do you recall any discussion of a sniper problem and Colonel Blaskic's recommendations on how to solve that sniper problem, or is that a subject that you simply have no recollection of whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I do recall there was -- I do remember the topic came up. I can't remember what was agreed or what we proposed, other than if we were going to take casualties, then we would respond accordingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a reference at the bottom of the first page of this military information summary to a joint commission for Bosnia and Herzegovina that is -- whose members are summarised on the bottom of the first page, as you can see. Do you have any knowledge regarding the positions held by these eight listed people, four on behalf of the ABiH and four on behalf of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I can't remember. I'm sure I did at the time, but they're just names now. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just two questions, if I can jog your memory. Does it ring a familar bell that the fourth person listed under the ABiH, Sefer Halilovic, was actually the commanding officer of all of the ABiH forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: If that was the case, I can't deny it, but I can't remember. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the fourth name under the HVO, Milivoj Petkovic; does it ring a bell that he was the chief of the general staff of the HVO in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Again, I'm sorry, I can't --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This might be a convenient time to break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Have you got very much more for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Perhaps 15 or 20 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Hay, we've both been asked by the interpreters to keep our voices up because they are having difficulty hearing us. Just a few final topics I would like to address with you. Turning to the Convoy of Joy incident that you've described, the Convoy of Joy proceeded through Croat-held territory in the midst of of an offensive launched by Muslim forces in the Travnik area; isn't that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, there was conflict going on at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, sir, in the summer of 1993, the Muslim forces launched a series of large-scale offensives against HVO forces in a variety of areas, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've already heard a lot of evidence on that, and I do not believe that it's necessary to burden the record any further with it, Major. But turning to the offensive in the Travnik area, that resulted in many thousands of refugees, Croats, who had been expelled from their homes; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, there -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And around the time of the Convoy of Joy, were you aware that there had been two separate massacres of Croat civilians, first in Maljina, where 36 Croat civilians were killed and 270 families cleaned out of their houses, and second in the village of Cukle, where 19 civilians were killed and 175 families expelled from their houses?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I cannot remember specifics, but yes, I do recall there was the term -- to use the term "cleansing" -- going on on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, sir, that that had a large part in the ugly mood demonstrated by the largely civilian crowd that apprehended the Convoy of Joy in the Novi Travnik area?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I'm sure it contributed to the feelings, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One final line of questions in this vein, sir: Were you aware that an artillery shell had been fired from Stari Vitez into Vitez, that it hit a children's playground in the evening of June the 10th of 1993 and actually killed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've heard a great deal of evidence about this. This witness ceased to be the liaison officer in June. I wonder if there is any point going over it again. We know that this happened; other witnesses have been asked about it, and it doesn't seem to me that repetition is going to assist us, unless there is a particular question relating to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I take your point acutely, Mr. President, and I only have one question in that regard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, did you ever hear of any investigation being initiated or conducted by ABiH forces responsible for the deaths of those eight children in Stari Vitez during the evening of June the 10th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: In Vitez?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Vitez, yes.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, but what I would say, at the time, the ABiH were in no position to conduct an investigation at that time, given their circumstances in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the detachment in Stari Vitez was a detachment of the 325th Mountain Brigade of the 3rd Corps, headquartered in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of any investigation being performed by the 3rd Corps, or by anyone on the ABiH side, into the events of that evening that we've just described?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The Convoy of Joy, sir, was a purely private convoy, I believe, not one which was sponsored by any United Nations organisations, such as the UNHCR or other U.N.-related organisations; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Correct. It was sponsored by themselves, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself see people, civilians, making a desperate grab for whatever they could grab from the convoy and carting things off in wheelbarrows and hand carts and things of that variety?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One question in connection with the death of the UNHCR driver that you testified about, sir, towards the end of your tour, killed by members, I believe you said, of the 7th Muslim Brigade: Do you recall whether members of that brigade were ever asked to conduct any investigations relating to that death and the circumstances of it?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, not -- not during my time. But that instance coincided very quickly with the 3rd BritBat coming in to take over from us, so they may have instigated an investigation. But I do recall a United Nations investigator coming over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was at the end of your tour, and I believe the Prince of Wales Own Regiment of Yorkshire was replaced as the BritBat component of UNPROFOR by the Coldstream Guards; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know whether the Coldstream Guards ever prevailed upon the 7th Muslim Brigade or the 3rd Corps to conduct their own internal investigation into that fatality, do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Correct. I -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a very brief line of questions about the Grbavica assault on September the 8th, 7th and the 8th. Isn't it true that immediately prior to the assault on the feature by the forces of the HVO that the civilians of Grbavica had requested the assistance of BritBat to be evacuated to Travnik?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I wasn't aware whether it was before or during, but I was aware that civilians, for their own protection, were evacuated through to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's my point precisely. Prior to -- in order to prevent civilian injuries or fatalities, a request for assistance was made to UNPROFOR, and BritBat, the Prince of Wales Own, actually conducted an armed escort of these civilians out of the war zone; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes. Once the -- when they had -- when battle had commenced, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a result of this, which is very understandable, there were no civilian casualties, were there --

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the time of the Grbavica assault, Major, there is no question that there was a huge refugee problem in Vitez and the surrounding area; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: There was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One component of that problem was the concomitant, if you like, of a severe housing shortage because of the large numbers of people flooding into the area; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, that's the way it was. I mean, ethnic sort of groups were coming together into their own sort of ethnic groups, from being displaced -- being displaced elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One final question: In connection with your visit to General Alagic, and the prisoners of war that you saw in the basement of his headquarters, you never actually saw these people again, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes the questions that I have for the major.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Bozidar Kovacic and I'm a lawyer from Rijeka, and I have colleague Goran Mikulicic from Zagreb, and together we represent represent Mr. Mario Cerkez, the second accused in this case. We don't speak the same language, so I should like to ask you to be kind enough to make a small pause before giving your answer to my questions, to facilitate the work of the interpreters. Also, if you don't understand my question, please let me know immediately. Major, during your tour of duty in Central Bosnia, you replaced your colleague, Matthew Dundas-Whatley, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And immediately after your arrival, you made a tour to familiarise yourself with a number of personalities on both sides, the HVO and the BH army, people who meant something, so as to be able to do your work properly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I infer from that that this was a process of preparation for your work and gathering of information on the subject that you had to deal with?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, it assisted in getting to know the local commanders, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, before your actual arrival in Bosnia, did you have any preliminary knowledge about the Balkans?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes, I had done a bit of book reading. I can't remember the books now, but yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major, when you arrived in the Lasva Valley, regardless of the briefings that you had had and your knowledge, was the situation black and white and clear, or were there many grey areas? What was your impression, your first impression when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It wasn't -- it wasn't your everyday circumstance. It was unusual, yes. It was -- things were going on that wouldn't normally go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the things that I believe you tried to grasp immediately was the question of the zones of responsibility and establishment of contact with local commanders in the areas in your area of responsibility. Did you obtain clear information of which commander, regardless of whether he was from the HVO or from the BH army, was responsible for which particular area?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: I had a working knowledge of who was -- of specific areas of responsibility and who were the notional commanders. But what you have to understand is that out there, at the time we arrived, the bomb had gone off in Vitez, Ahmici had happened, and a variety of other incidents had happened, and what you and I would interpret as a normal existence did not -- was not extant out there at the time. Furthermore, regarding your question, there were a lot of provincial, local individuals who may have been doing things on their own without the consent, knowledge, or whatever, of their hierarchy, on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But can we agree that from the standpoint of your responsibilities, it was your constant task to establish which unit, which area of responsibility, which assignment each particular unit had?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: As far as I could -- as far as we could, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Major, at the beginning of your examination-in-chief, I believe it must have been a lapsus linguae by the Prosecutor when it was stated that the base of the British was in Nova Bila. I assume that you know that the location was Stara Bila or Bila, not Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: It was at the school in Nova Bila --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Okay. I can't remember, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try and remind you. During your stay there, you must have visited the hospital in Nova Bila, the hospital in the church, the improvised hospital in the church in Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: No, I didn't visit it. That was the G-5 LO who used to do that. I can't remember visiting a hospital in a church, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But during your daily meetings of liaison officers that you referred to, did you know from that that there was an improvised HVO hospital in a church in Nova Bila?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: There were numerous improvised hospitals. I remember visiting one in Vitez itself, but I can't remember exactly what building it was in. As I say, there were a couple of improvised hospitals. I can't remember any specific one, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The hospital you mentioned in Vitez, are you thinking of the town itself?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe that, conditionally speaking, hospital was actually in a basement, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, Major, in the course of your stay in Central Bosnia, could you at least roughly tell us how many times you had occasion to meet with Mr. Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
utterances.text: Again, not more than ten times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume this was mostly in the initial period, before you had divided your area of responsibility with another colleague.

utterances.speaker: ANGUS HAY
